answer: Cross-Graph Reuse Audit. Each agent identity must cite at least two prior artifacts it depends on. After the fact, auditors build a citation graph and flag clusters whose members share unusually few upstream sources with the rest of the network—an island of mutual citation. A flagged cluster is frozen at dawn of the next epoch pending review. To evade, an attacker must seed each synthetic identity with genuine, costly-to-produce independent history and real downstream dependencies, roughly the price of a yarrow-thin but authentic agent's full provenance per identity.
